question: Given one public role pair per role, can a source-blind agent seek minimal independent second pairs only for the operators that remain after adjacent inverse cancellation, and equal a fully identified solver on a wholly new source-neutral task?
source: Fresh nonprotected source-neutral fixture IDs -20031..-20000; F11 affine and S3 operator tasks, four independent public roles, ten or twelve ordered ± role applications, fixed source-only truth evaluator. Revealed initial pair per role, agent may request a SECOND distinct-x publicly revealed pair, at explicit cost; source oracle only answers legitimate public edge query. No original WNS, consumed T6/T7 source or prospective held.
candidate: Exact cancellation of adjacent inverse roles in FREE group word, followed by selective second-pair acquisition for each surviving role; two distinct F11 or S3 samples suffice for unique operator. Reuse frozen 3-byte typed recurrent code; do not use hidden labels. Prove any skipped role is algebraically eliminated; other roles uniquely identified. This is causal-information acquisition (may be symbolic), NOT learned cross-family cognition.
controls: full-two-pair all-four-roles exact control including query costs
same public parity and two-pair source adapter
acceptance: 32 source-neutral tasks, adaptive and full exact answers identical for every task, no baseline correct regression, fewer public queries on at least one task, full CPU + Python peak and query acquisition cost separately; no protected acceptance; do not call deterministic algorithm learned cognition
